rag.description: CopyFiles copies files, folders, or wildcard matches to a local or shared destination with cp-style rules. Paths can come from macros or data columns, and NoClobber protects existing files. A missing source fails the step, and the copied and skipped paths are reported so later steps can verify the result.

qa.question: What is the CopyFiles plugin?
qa.answer: CopyFiles is an action that copies a file, a directory, or a wildcard pattern to a destination, mirroring the cp and copy commands.

qa.question: Which parameters does CopyFiles support?
qa.answer: Source and Destination are required. Recursive includes all subfolders, and NoClobber skips files that already exist at the destination.

qa.question: Where can CopyFiles run in a G4 environment?
qa.answer: CopyFiles runs on the machine that executes the automation, so it applies when the G4 Hub or worker and the automation share a machine or can both reach a shared location such as a UNC share. Documentation: https://github.com/g4-api/g4-plugins/blob/main/docs/Actions/CopyFiles.md Source: https://github.com/g4-api/g4-plugins/blob/main/src/G4.Plugins.Common/Actions/CopyFiles.cs

qa.question: How do I make sure CopyFiles copies into a folder instead of renaming the file?
qa.answer: End Destination with a directory separator or point it to an existing folder. Any other destination path becomes the new file or folder name.

qa.question: How is a CopyFiles rule defined and where are its results stored?
qa.answer: Use an ActionRuleModel with pluginName CopyFiles and an argument such as {{$ --Source:C:\Reports\report.pdf --Destination:C:\Archive\}}. The session parameters CopyFiles:Count and CopyFiles:Files hold the copied count and a JSON array of destination paths, and the entity also lists Skipped paths.

qa.question: What is the CopyFiles manifest version and author?
qa.answer: The manifest version is 4 and the author is Roei Sabag.

qa.question: How does the CopyFiles manifest summarize the plugin?
qa.answer: It copies a file, a directory, or a wildcard pattern with cp-style rules, supports recursive copies and NoClobber, and reports the copied count and paths.

qa.question: What happens when CopyFiles fails?
qa.answer: The step fails when Source or Destination is empty, the source does not exist, the pattern folder does not exist, or access is denied. Files copied before an error stay in place, while a pattern that matches nothing succeeds with a count of zero.

description: ### Purpose
Copies a file, a directory, or a wildcard pattern to a destination, mirroring the `cp` and `copy` commands.
It runs on the machine that executes the automation, so it applies when the G4 Hub or worker and the automation share a machine or can both reach a shared physical location.
### Key Features and Functionality
| Feature            | Description                                                                                               |
| Single File Copy   | Copies one file onto a new file name, or into an existing folder or a path ending with a separator.       |
| Directory Copy     | Copies the top-level files of a directory, or the complete tree including empty folders with `Recursive`. |
| Wildcard Patterns  | Copies files that match `*` and `?` in the last `Source` segment into the `Destination` folder.           |
| Recursive Patterns | Matches the pattern in every subfolder with `Recursive` and keeps the relative folder structure.          |
| Overwrite Control  | Overwrites existing files by default and preserves them when `NoClobber` is present.                      |
| Path Resolution    | Accepts absolute, UNC, and relative paths; relative paths resolve from the process working directory.     |
| Result Reporting   | Publishes the copied count and paths to the session and the copied and skipped paths to the entity.       |
| Hidden Files       | Copies hidden and system files like any other file, matching the behavior of `cp`.                        |
### Usages in RPA
| Use Case             | Description                                                                            |
| Report Distribution  | Copies generated reports or exports to a shared folder where other teams pick them up. |
| Input Staging        | Copies source files into a working folder before a process reads or transforms them.   |
| Backup Before Change | Copies files to a backup folder with `NoClobber` before a step modifies the originals. |
### Usages in Automation Testing
| Use Case            | Description                                                                              |
| Test Data Setup     | Copies fixture files or folders into the location the application under test reads from. |
| Artifact Collection | Gathers logs, screenshots, or downloads into one folder after a test run.                |
| Result Archiving    | Copies a complete results tree to a network share for later review.                      |
### Destination Rules
| Source    | Destination Exists As Folder              | Destination Does Not Exist                            |
| File      | Copied into the folder with its own name. | Copied to the destination as the new file name.       |
| Directory | Copied into the folder as a child folder. | The destination becomes the copied folder.            |
| Pattern   | Matches are copied into the folder.       | The folder is created when at least one file matches. |
### Failure Behavior
1. An empty `Source` or `Destination` stops the action.
2. A missing source file or directory stops the action.
3. A missing folder that hosts a wildcard pattern stops the action.
4. A pattern that matches no files succeeds and reports a count of zero.
5. Files copied before an error, such as denied access, stay at the destination.
The number of files copied by the action.
Files skipped because of `NoClobber` are not counted.
entity.name: Count

description: A JSON array of the destination paths of every copied file.
The same value is stored in the session as `CopyFiles:Files`.
entity.name: Files

description: A JSON array of the destination paths preserved because `NoClobber` is present.
The array is empty when `NoClobber` is absent or no target file existed.
entity.name: Skipped

edge_cases: A destination ending with a separator is treated as a folder
An existing destination file is overwritten
annotations.expected_result: The file report.pdf is copied to C:\Archive\report-copy.pdf and CopyFiles:Count is 1.
annotations.notes: Destination is treated as the new file name because it is not an existing folder and does not end with a separator.

description: ### Copy a single file to a new name
Bind `Source` to a file and `Destination` to a path that does not exist as a folder.
CopyFiles writes the file to that path and creates any missing parent folders.

edge_cases: An existing destination folder receives a child folder named after the source
annotations.expected_result: The complete Results tree, including empty folders, is copied to the shared location.
annotations.notes: Recursive copies every subfolder. The UNC share must be reachable from the machine that executes the automation.

description: ### Copy a directory tree to a network share
Enable `Recursive` to copy a directory with all of its subfolders.
CopyFiles mirrors the tree, including empty folders, at the shared destination.

edge_cases: A pattern that matches nothing succeeds with a count of zero
Destination is always treated as a folder
annotations.expected_result: Every .log file under C:\Logs, including subfolders, is copied to C:\Collected while existing targets are listed in Skipped.
annotations.notes: Wildcards are supported only in the last Source segment. Recursive keeps the relative folder structure of the matches.

description: ### Collect log files without overwriting existing copies
Use a wildcard pattern with `Recursive` to gather matching files from every subfolder.
Enable `NoClobber` so files that already exist at the destination are skipped and reported.

edge_cases: An existing output folder receives a child folder named input
Relative paths resolve from the process working directory
annotations.expected_result: When the output folder does not exist, it is created and receives the top-level files of the input folder.
annotations.notes: A directory source without Recursive copies only its top-level files.

description: ### Copy top-level files using relative paths
Provide relative `Source` and `Destination` paths to resolve them from the process working directory.
Without `Recursive`, CopyFiles copies only the files at the top level of the source directory.
The number of files copied by the action.
Files skipped because of `NoClobber` are not counted.
outputParameters.name: CopyFiles:Count

description: A JSON array of the destination paths of every copied file.
It can be referenced by downstream rules, for example to assert or process each copied file.
outputParameters.name: CopyFiles:Files

description: The source file, directory, or wildcard pattern to copy.
Wildcards `*` and `?` are supported only in the last path segment.
Absolute, UNC, and relative paths are accepted; relative paths resolve from the process working directory.
parameters.name: Source

description: The target file or folder using cp-style rules.
An existing folder or a path ending with a separator receives the copy; any other path becomes the new name.
Missing parent folders are created.
parameters.name: Destination

description: Copies directories with all subfolders, including empty ones, when present.
With a wildcard pattern, it also matches files in every subfolder and keeps their relative structure.
parameters.name: Recursive

description: Skips files that already exist at the destination instead of overwriting them when present.
Skipped destination paths are reported in the entity `Skipped` field.
parameters.name: NoClobber

description: Provides the `Source`, `Destination`, `Recursive`, and `NoClobber` parameters through a G4 parameter expression.
Values can come from macros or data columns, so one rule can copy different paths in each run.
properties.name: Argument

summary: Copies a file, a directory, or a wildcard pattern to a destination using cp-style rules.
Supports recursive copies, overwrites existing files unless NoClobber is present, and creates missing folders.
Reports the copied count and destination paths through the session and the response entity.
